insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose 22% to ₹4,949 Cr with reported EBITDA of ₹827 Cr and PAT nearly doubling to ₹329 Cr, as OFC exports (41% of revenue, up from 12%) took off. The order book hit ₹21,200 Cr, including a ~$1.1 billion long-term OFC contract and ₹12,250 Cr of exports. The MD expects 20-25% revenue growth and a 3-4 point higher EBITDA margin in FY27 (calling it an expectation, not guidance), plus ₹400 Cr from new data-centre interconnect products and a defence push including an aerospace acquisition.

what_changed.text: FY27: 20-25% revenue growth and 3-4 points higher EBITDA margin (expectation)
$1.1 billion long-term OFC supply contract; order book ₹21,200 Cr
₹580 Cr preform plant (300 t) for backward integration
Aerospace acquisition into HFCL Advance Systems with ~₹1,930 Cr export order book

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: This quarter and financial year mark a defining milestone for HFCL

analyst_questions.answer: No formal guidance; 20-25% revenue growth and 3-4 points of margin expansion 'expected'.
Due to unpaid warranty work on the Army network; AMC (~₹170 Cr a year) expected from Q2; BharatNet profitable.
Prices have risen sharply, partly from drone demand (which HFCL does not supply); MD thinks they are near the top.
Fibre at 100% use; HFCL keeps some capacity for spot orders, which earn more.

red_flags.text: Receivables above ₹2,000 Cr; MD could not split EPC or overdue amounts on the call.
EPC segment loss-making on the Army network warranty.
Equity dilution via promoter warrants and defence restructuring (subsidiary stakes).
Electronic fuzes needed upgrades after trials.

watch_next: Fibre and cable capacity additions by December

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Optical fibre and cables (incl. high-fibre-count IBR), data-centre connectivity, telecom equipment, defence products (radars, thermal sights, fuzes), and EPC for telecom networks
business_snapshot.customers: Global telecom and data-centre buyers (exports >70% of cable output), Indian telcos, BharatNet, Indian Army
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: exports 41%, products 62%; telecom products 66% of Q4 revenue
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: AI data centres in the US, fibre price increases, defence indigenisation, BharatNet
